THE WORKLIST FOR SPLITTING A LAKE INTO THE WATERS THE BOOK TREATS IT AS.

A lake belongs here when two or more synopsis rows resolve to the SAME registry item and name different PARTS of it — an arm, a bay, a reach. `matched` is what decides that, not the bundle's `entry.item_id`, which keeps only the first of a row's items.

It is deliberately NOT every sub-area a rule mentions. Sixty-seven rules in the corpus name a place inside a water and bind to all of it; almost all are one closure between one pair of boundary signs, and those are marked on the row (`widened`) rather than cut.

HOW A POLYGON LANDS. Add a feature to `data/curated/waters/added_lakes.geojson` with the reserved `id` below and a ring in EPSG:4326. `wbk` and `gnis_id` are DERIVED from `id` and must not be authored. On the next atlas build the ingest re-stamps every fid inside the ring to the new lake key — which cuts those fids out of the original lake and mints the `lake:{wbk}` boundary the rule binds to. The base polygon is replaced by the split ones as a consequence; nothing has to remove it.

lakes.note: Four rows on one lake: one for ALL PARTS and one for each of the three. The zone entry `z4:kootenay_lake_boundaries` states where the lines fall, and the synopsis prints the map on page 34. Today every one of them covers all 423 km².

_sweep: Re-run after every parse. The test is: two or more rows whose `matched` includes the same item, where at least one row's NAME qualifies the lake with a part word (arm, bay, reach, main body, zone, netted off). Twenty-three lakes carry more than one row on one item; the other twenty are a lake plus its tributaries, one row written in two regions, an alias pair ("JONES" LAKE / WAHLEACH LAKE), or — worth a look — two genuinely different lakes matched to one polygon, which is a curation bug rather than a polygon job: BIG LAKE (west of 100 Mile House) and BIG LAKE (west of Likely) both resolve to wbk:329480768, and the two BLUE LAKEs to wbk:329413147.
